title: Enable Indexes
description: Learn how to rebuild and re-enable disabled indexes using ALTER INDEX, CREATE INDEX, and DBCC DBREINDEX.

data.text: After disabling an index (e.g., before a bulk update), you need to rebuild it to re-enable it. You cannot simply enable a disabled index — it must be rebuilt.

data.title: Rebuild a single index
data.content: Rebuilds a disabled index to make it usable again.

data.title: Rebuild all disabled indexes
data.content: Rebuilds all disabled indexes on the table.
data.code:
ALTER INDEX ALL ON table_name
REBUILD;

data.title: Recreate index with DROP_EXISTING
data.content: Recreates the index, replacing the disabled one.

data.title: DBCC DBREINDEX syntax
data.content: Rebuilds an index using the legacy DBCC DBREINDEX command.

data.text: A rebuild is a full drop-and-create of the index behind the scenes, so it recovers fragmentation and refreshes statistics at the same time. The most useful options are `ONLINE = ON` (Enterprise) to avoid blocking writers, `FILLFACTOR` to leave free space on each page, and `SORT_IN_TEMPDB` to move the sort work off the target database's data file.

data.title: Rebuild with options
data.content: Run against a real table (temp tables do not support ONLINE builds in every version).
data.code:
-- Rebuild a single index without holding write locks for the whole build
ALTER INDEX ix_orders_customer ON dbo.Orders
    REBUILD WITH (ONLINE = ON, FILLFACTOR = 90, SORT_IN_TEMPDB = ON);

-- Inspect fragmentation and page counts for every index on a table
SELECT
    i.name                          AS index_name,
    i.type_desc,
    ps.avg_fragmentation_in_percent AS fragmentation_pct,
    ps.page_count
FROM sys.dm_db_index_physical_stats(DB_ID(), OBJECT_ID('dbo.Orders'), NULL, NULL, 'SAMPLED') AS ps
JOIN sys.indexes AS i ON i.object_id = ps.object_id AND i.index_id = ps.index_id
WHERE ps.index_level = 0
ORDER BY ps.avg_fragmentation_in_percent DESC;

data.title: When to rebuild
data.text: A common rule of thumb: rebuild above roughly 30% fragmentation, reorganise between 5% and 30%, and leave below 5% alone. Always check `page_count` first — rebuilding a 10-page index costs more than it saves.

data.title: Enable Index Key Points
points: Disabled indexes must be rebuilt, not simply enabled.
Use ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD for the standard approach.
CREATE INDEX WITH (DROP_EXISTING=ON) can also rebuild a disabled index.
DBCC DBREINDEX is a legacy command still available for compatibility.
